entry.title: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ for even $n$: rigid sequences, products, and growth beyond Harborth's bound
entry.summary: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ and $η(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. For even $n$, Harborth's construction gives $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+1$, with equality when $n$ is a power of two. Wang and Zeng recently showed that this bound is strict for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n$ that is not a power of two, with an excess of $2^{r-3}(m-1)$, where $m$ is the odd part of $n$; this disproves Properties C and D. We show that the excess grows faster than $2^r$. For every even $n=2^am$ with odd $m\ge3$ and every $r\ge4$, \[ s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+(m-1)\,2^{r-3}\lfloor r/4\rfloor+1 , \] so that $s(C_n^r)-2^r(n-1)\ge c_n\,r\,2^r$.

entry.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
entry.summary: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

entry.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
entry.summary: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.

entry.title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
entry.summary: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg's universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.

entry.title: On the Hasse principle for a block-diagonal form and a form of lower degree
entry.summary: We investigate the Hasse principle for systems consisting of one form of degree $k$ which decomposes as a sum of $n$-ary forms, and one general form of degree $d < k$. By exploiting the block structure of the first form before applying Weyl differencing, we refine the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this setting; in particular, for a sum of binary quartic forms and a quadratic form, the requirement $s > 516$ is relaxed to $s > 96$, which also improves on the bound $s > 100$ available for general forms.

entry.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
entry.summary: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

entry.title: Modular Existential Closedness
entry.summary: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(τ_1, \ldots, τ_n, j(τ_1), \ldots, j(τ_n)) \in V$ with $τ_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouché's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

entry.title: Re-Ordering the Generalized Hofstadter Functions G, H, and Beyond
entry.summary: Hofstadter's G function is recursively defined via G(0) = 0 and then G(n) = n-G(G(n -1)). Following Hofstadter, we vary the number k of nested recursive calls in this equation and obtain a family of functions (F\_k). In a previous article, we proved that this family is ordered pointwise: for all k and n, we have $F_k(n) $le$ F_{k+1}(n)$. Here we propose a much shorter proof of this theorem, without infinite morphic words. The key ingredient for this direct proof is a new formula expressing iterates of the preimages of $F_k$ . Thanks to this formula, we also prove several conjectures mentioned in our previous article. In particular we obtain that $F_k(n) < F_{k+1}(n)$ when n > (k + 1)(k + 6)/2. We provide a certified formalization of all these results in the Rocq proof assistant.

entry.title: Spectral zeta functions in positive characteristic
entry.summary: Spectral zeta functions and zeta-regularized determinants encode the spectrum of an operator in analytic functions. Over the completion $\mathbb C_\infty$ of an algebraic closure of $\mathbb F_q((π))$, two features of characteristic $p$ break this classical picture. Complex powers have exponents that vary only continuously in $\mathbb Z_p$, not analytically. Scalar traces record eigenvalue multiplicities only modulo $p$. We develop a resolvent-based theory that treats these two obstructions separately. For the first, inverse Stieltjes duality turns suitable scalar resolvents into locally analytic spectral distributions on $\mathbb F_q[[π]]$. A single exponent of the Mellin transform already determines the distribution and the entire Mellin family. We characterize exactly which power series arise in this way, by a growth condition on Carlitz moments. The criterion depends on the support: bounded Taylor coefficients are not sufficient. For stationary digit measures, the transform is the unique fixed point of an explicit contraction. The first $q-1$ nonconstant moments recover the measure. For the second, we replace traces by the Frobenius defect $F/σ(F)$, where $σ$ raises coefficients to their $q$th powers. On power series with small coefficients, this map is a group automorphism that preserves Gauss distances, and a convergent infinite product inverts it. Polynomial defects produce entire functions. They characterize exactly the diagonal spectra that are finite unions of forward Frobenius orbits, counted with multiplicity. For the shifted Carlitz operator, the resulting Fredholm determinant is a normalized reciprocal of the Anderson--Thakur function, and its Newton polygon is determined exactly.

entry.title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
entry.summary: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $α$, let $λ_{k,α}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24λ_{k,α}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^α}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^αn+λ_{k,α}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(α+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.

entry.title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
entry.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.

entry.title: Bounds on the number of squares in recurrence sequences: $y_{0}=b^{2}$ (II)
entry.summary: For binary recurrence sequences, $\left( y_{k} \right)_{k \in \bbZ}$, arising from the solutions of generalised Pell equations, $X^{2}-dY^{2}=c$, where $y_{0}$ is any positive square and $c=-2^{\ell}p^{m}$ for an odd prime $p$ and non-negative integers $\ell$ and $m$, we show that there are at most $4$ distinct squares with $y_{k}$ sufficiently large. From this result, we also show that there are at most $7$ distinct squares when $y_{0}=1,2^{2},\ldots,7^{2}$, or once $d$ exceeds an explicit lower bound, without any conditions on the size of such squares.
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: Research in Number Theory, volume 12, article 6 (2026)

entry.title: Weighted density bounds for covering systems over Dedekind domains
entry.summary: We study the density of uncovered sets arising from finite families of residue classes over Dedekind domains with finite residue norms. Building on the distortion method of Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba, we prove a general weighted density criterion in which the weight attached to a prime ideal is allowed to vary. In the critical Mertens regime this yields, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the admissible prime-ideal weight \[ 1+\frac{(\log N\mathfrak p)^3(\log\log N\mathfrak p)^{1+\varepsilon}}{N\mathfrak p}, \] up to a harmless modification at finitely many small prime ideals. This is asymptotically smaller than the fixed weight \(1+(\log N\mathfrak p)^{3+\varepsilon}/N\mathfrak p\) appearing in the earlier density theorem. The result is valid for systems of any fixed multiplicity and, for multiplicity one, requires the ideal moduli themselves to be distinct but not their norms. We then place the analytic hypotheses in Knopfmacher's Axiom~A framework. In the critical case of Axiom~A with exponent \(1\), the prime-ideal estimates needed by the weighted theorem are automatic. More generally, under Axiom~A with exponent \(ρ>0\), we prove a weighted mean-value theorem on ideals; in the subcritical range \(0<ρ<1\), a first-moment argument shows that sufficiently large moduli cover an arbitrarily small proportion of the ambient space. We also explain that the distortion construction itself only uses a compatible system of finite residue spaces with uniform fibres and a Chinese-remainder-type product structure, suggesting a possible extension beyond Dedekind domains. Finally, we show that a direct passage from the second moment to higher integer moments does not lower the logarithmic exponent \(3\) within this moment hierarchy.

entry.title: Galois groups of polynomials over a fixed number field: determinant methods in general boxes, resolvents, and quantitative counting
entry.summary: Let $K$ be a fixed number field of degree $d$. We prove two determinant-method results for integral points over $\mathcal O_K$ in boxes whose coordinates may have different size bounds: a Bombieri-Pila type estimate for affine plane curves that retains the two separate coordinate bounds, and a Salberger-Browning covering theorem for affine surfaces. If $F\in\mathcal O_K[X_1,X_2]$ is irreducible and $T=\max B_1^{e_1}B_2^{e_2}$ over the monomials occurring in $F$, then \[ N_K(F;B_1,B_2)\ll T^\varepsilon \exp\!\left(d\frac{\log B_1\log B_2}{\log T}\right). \] For an absolutely irreducible surface in three variables we obtain a covering by $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K})$ bounded-degree auxiliary hypersurfaces, outside $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K}^2)$ exceptional integral points, where \[ V_{3,K}=\exp\!\left(d \left(\frac{\log B_1\log B_2\log B_3}{\log T}\right)^{1/2}\right). \] These are the number-field analogues of determinant-method estimates for unequal coordinate ranges developed in the rational setting by Browning and Heath-Brown, Salberger, Browning, and Chow-Dietmann. We then apply them to Galois resolvents of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $K$. Independently, a large-sieve argument, in the tradition of Gallagher's probabilistic Galois theory, gives $O_{K,n}(N^{dn-d/2}\log N)$ exceptional separable polynomials, while effective Hilbert irreducibility over global fields gives subgroup-sensitive bounds with exponent $d(n-1+1/[S_n:G])$, up to logarithms. We record the interaction with the discriminant-square equation for even groups, congruence restrictions, and rectangular coefficient boxes. All determinant estimates used in the applications are proved in the paper; no conjectural global-field determinant statement is assumed.

entry.title: On almost perfect additive complements
entry.summary: Let $A, B$ be infinite sets of non-negative integers with $n\in A+B$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. We prove that if $A(x)B(x)-x$ does not tend to infinity, then $$\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\in\Big[\frac{3}{2}, 2\Big].$$ The lower bound is sharp, and confirms a conjecture of Chen. Our proof is based on the weak limits and the convolution factorization theorem of Gabardo and Lai. A discrete proof of the same bound was also given by Zhang. Motivated by the known spectrum of perfect additive complements, we conjecture that the interval $(3/2, 8/5)$ is also excluded for almost perfect additive complements.

entry.title: Non-liftability of the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension
entry.summary: Let $p\geq3$ be a prime number. We prove that the action of the Galois group on the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension $\mathbf{Q}_p\left(ζ_{p^\infty},p^{1/p^\infty}\right)$ of $\mathbf{Q}_p$ is not liftable to its Cohen ring with respect to any admissible coefficient field.

entry.title: Counting Integral Matrices with Given Cubic Characteristic Polynomial
entry.summary: We show that the number of $3\times 3$ matrices with given characteristic polynomial and entries in $\mathbb{Z}\cap [-H,H]$ is at most $c H^{3}(\log H)^{6}$ for all $H\ge 2$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

entry.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
entry.summary: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.

entry.title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
entry.summary: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.

entry.title: The Family $X_{qp^s}$ for Distinct Primes $q,p$ in Connection with Carmichael's Totient Conjecture
entry.summary:
Shannon, Shiue, Saito and the author \cite{SSHS2025} studied the sets $X_k=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\varphi(n)=k\}$ in connection with Carmichael's totient conjecture, and proved that for an odd prime $p
eq3$ and $s\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, $X_{2p^s}$ is empty whenever $2p^s+1$ is not prime (with $s=1$ fully characterized in both directions), conjecturing that this persists for every $s\ge1$. We resolve that conjecture in full, obtaining a complete characterization of $X_{2p^s}$ for every $s\ge1$ and every odd prime $p
eq3$, together with a parity dichotomy: $X_{2p^s}=\varnothing$ unconditionally whenever $s$ is even, while for odd $s$ both outcomes genuinely occur, determined exactly by the primality of $2p^s+1$. We then close the one remaining gap at $p=3$, where the proof technique degenerates, with a separate, unconditional characterization of $X_{2\cdot3^s}$. Building on these results, we consider the natural generalization $X_{qp^s}$, where $q
eq p$ are distinct primes and $s\ge1$. We show that this generalization splits into three cases of very different character. If $q$ and $p$ are both odd, the problem is trivial: $qp^s$ is odd, so $X_{qp^s}=\varnothing$ by elementary parity, with no case-analysis needed. If $q=2$, the problem is exactly the family $X_{2p^s}$ resolved above. If $p=2$, giving the ``mirror'' family $X_{2^sq}$ for an odd prime $q$, the problem is genuinely different. Beyond $s=1$, we give a complete resolution for $s=2$, recovering, with an explicit proof and solution sets, the qualitative dichotomy of \cite[Thm.~2.3.1]{SSHS2025}, but the problem remains open for $s\ge3$.

entry.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
entry.summary: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $Δ(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $Δ(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

entry.title: Finiteness theorems for trace Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields
entry.summary: Motivated by Clark's work on Euclidean quadratic forms, we introduce trace Euclidean and house Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields, and relate these concepts through the $p$-norm Euclidean property. We prove that, as $F$ varies over all totally real number fields of arbitrary degree, there are only finitely many positive definite trace Euclidean $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattices of arbitrary rank $n\ge1$, up to isometry. For every $p\in[1,\infty]$, the same finiteness holds for positive definite $p$-norm Euclidean lattices. We also classify all positive definite trace Euclidean lattices of rank one over real quadratic fields: there are exactly six isometry classes, and every such lattice is free. As a corollary, the trace Euclidean real quadratic fields are precisely $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{13})$.

entry.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
entry.summary: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

entry.title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
entry.summary: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-28}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.

entry.title: Frangible prime gaps
entry.summary: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erdős. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.7416, 2.7984]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

entry.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$
entry.summary: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/π^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Apéry-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.

entry.title: On real biquadratic number fields for which the $2$-Iwasawa module has rank $3$
entry.summary: We investigate the stability of the $2$-rank in the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of real biquadratic number fields. We determine several families of real biquadratic fields $F$ for which the ranks of the $2$-class group $A(F)$ and the associated $2$-Iwasawa module $A_\infty(F)$ are both equal to $3$. More precisely, we provide a complete classification of all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d$ is an odd positive square-free integer, and all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is a positive square-free integer, for which $ \operatorname{rank}(A(F))=\operatorname{rank}(A_\infty(F))=3.$

entry.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
entry.summary: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(eπn)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},μ)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_μ(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)ψ(αn)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $μ$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $ψ$ is $1$-periodic and real-analytic, and $α$ has irrationality exponent smaller than $1+\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}(P)+1}$. On the one hand, the latter assumption is satisfied by a.e. $α\in\mathbb{R}$, and, on the other hand, our result covers any of the following concrete orbits \[ \lfloor n\cos(eπn)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\lfloor n^{37}\sin(n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\big\lfloor \sqrt{2}n^{10}e^{\sin(π(\sqrt[5]{7}+1) n)}\big\rfloor\text{,}\quad \big\lfloor \big((\log 2) n^3+e n\big)e^{e^{\cos(π\sqrt{2} n)}}\big\rfloor\text{.} \] The proof employs the so-called one-frequency circle method for estimating exponential sums with phases $\big(ξ\lfloor P(n)ψ(αn)\rfloor\big)_{1\le n\le N}$, but the major arc approximants of our exponential sums do not consist of their direct continuous counterparts. In the major arc regime we decouple the $ψ$-oscillatory part of the phase from the polynomial one, and approximate the exponential sum by $\int_0^1\big(\frac{1}{N}\int_0^Ne^{2πiξP(t)ψ( s)}dt\big)ds$. This represents a novel phenomenon for problems of this kind, and, interestingly, our proof exploits the coefficient-free variational estimates of Radon-type operators.

entry.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
entry.summary: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.

entry.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
entry.summary: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.

entry.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
entry.summary: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

entry.title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
entry.summary: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps. We introduce generalized cubic partitions and discover the minimal excludant, as well as several additional results.

entry.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the Néron--Severi Group
entry.summary: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the Néron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. The proof combines the Diophantine-approximation method of Ziyang Gao and the author (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22285) with Lefschetz fibrations. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.

entry.title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
entry.summary: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{χ_{δ_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $δ_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $χ_{δ_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.

entry.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
entry.summary: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $ξ_0,\dots,ξ_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2ξ_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}ξ_0^2ξ_1+ξ_0ξ_4-ξ_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

entry.title: Explicit Coleman integration over finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
entry.summary: Coleman integration is an important computational ingredient of the Chabauty--Coleman method and its extensions. We extend the Balakrishnan--Tuitman algorithm to general smooth projective curves with good reduction over arbitrary finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, allowing both ramification and nontrivial residue degree. Given a suitable plane model and integral bases, we provide explicit precision bounds and an accompanying Magma implementation. As an application, a single-prime computation at $p=19$ over the unramified quadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}_{19^2}/\mathbb{Q}_{19}$ recovers all $35$ affine sporadic quadratic divisors on $X(s3,ns5)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Completeness is proved in an appendix using symmetric Chabauty and a Mordell--Weil sieve.

entry.title: Exploring topological features of a complex network of prime factors and composite numbers
entry.summary: Prime numbers are mathematical concepts of particular interest because of their relative rarity among integers, as well as the relative unpredictability of their occurrence and density along the integer sequence. They constitute the building blocks of all other composite numbers, giving rise to the interesting and important concept of prime factorization, a process guaranteed by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Among the several works that have been reported about prime numbers and their interrelationship with composite numbers, some have considered derived graphs and/or networks. In this paper, we derive some topological features of a bipartite complex network of prime factors and composite numbers. More specifically, we prove mathematically that the network's diameter is exactly five regardless of the number of nodes. In particular, we show that certain nontrivial sub-networks have minimal diameter equal to four, which is, again, independent of the number of nodes as long as the network is large enough. The last shows that this network is of small-world type. We also characterize exactly the number of boundary nodes in the network and present a couple of algorithms to identify the most important, relevant, influential, or central nodes of the network. Finally, we focus on the computation of the information dimensions on the basis of Shannon and Tsallis entropies of the studied complex network. The results show both decreasing as the number of nodes increases. Furthermore, both entropies indicate that box coverings at the diameters \(\varepsilon=[3,4]\), group nodes into roughly the same number of boxes, independent of the number of nodes in the network.

entry.title: Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves
entry.summary: Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\leκ\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $κ$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.

entry.title: Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
entry.summary: Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$. Andrews proved that $A_r(n)=B_r(n)$ for all positive integers $r$ and nonnegative integers $n$, thereby recovering MacMahon's identity as the special case $r=1$. We derive generating functions and asymptotic formulas for the total numbers of hooks of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$ in both partition classes, employing Wright's circle method. These asymptotic formulas yield several hook length bias results. In particular, for sufficiently large $n$, the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $1$-hooks than the $A_r$-type partitions, whereas for hook lengths $2$ and $3$, the bias is reversed when $r=1$ and favors the $B_r$-type partitions when $r\geq 2$. We also establish asymptotic inequalities among hook numbers of different lengths within each partition class. Finally, for fixed hook lengths $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$, we prove that the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $\ell$-hooks than the $B_{r+1}$-type partitions for sufficiently large $n$. These results reveal systematic asymptotic patterns in the distribution of small hook lengths across the two partition families.

entry.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
entry.summary: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.

entry.title: Zassenhaus Filtrations and Golod-Shafarevich Methods for Ihara Constants
entry.summary: Let $X$ be a curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Denote by $N(X)$ and $g(X)$ the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and the genus of $X$ respectively. The Ihara constant \begin{equation*} A(q)=\limsup_{g(X)\to\infty}\frac{N(X)}{g(X)} \end{equation*} measures the asymptotic abundance of rational points on curves over $\mathbb{F}_q$. It is a central problem in the study of algebraic geometry and has also attracted broader mathematical interest. In particular, the constant $A(2)$ is discussed in the \emph{Optimization Constants in Mathematics} collection maintained by Terence Tao et al \cite[Number 33]{DIT26}. In this paper, we study the Zassenhaus filtration of pro-$p$ groups arising from class field towers. By combining Golod--Shafarevich theorem, embedding problems and central class field theory, we establish a new criterion for the infinitude of class field towers. As an application, we obtain an improvement on the best known lower bounds of Ihara constant $A(2)$ and $A(3)$ which are explicitly given by \[ A(2)\geq 0.317779\cdots \text{ and } A(3)\geq 0.496074\cdots. \]

entry.title: On Lehmer's Problem
entry.summary: Let $m\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $d\geq 2$ be an even integer. We study monic, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic polynomials $$ P(x)=x^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_1x+1\in\mathbb{Z}[x]. $$ For a fixed residue class $r\in\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$, we prove that there exists an effectively computable constant $c_{r,m}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{r,m} $$ for every irreducible polynomial $Q$ whose inner coefficients satisfy $$ a_j\equiv r\pmod m \qquad (1\leq j\leq d-1). $$ Moreover, we explicitly compute the constant $c_{r,m}$ in terms of $r$ and $m$. For the residue classes $r=2$, $r=3$, and $r=m-1$, we obtain improved lower bounds for suitable ranges of the modulus~$m$. We also consider monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials whose inner coefficients belong to two distinct residue classes modulo $m$. More precisely, if the inner coefficients with odd indices are congruent to $a\pmod m$ and those with even indices are congruent to $b\pmod m$, where $a\not\equiv b\pmod m$, then we prove the existence of a constant $c_{m,a,b}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{m,a,b}. $$ These results solve Lehmer's problem for several families of polynomials. We also construct infinitely many examples in every even degree $d\geq 2$ of monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$, together with explicit information about their Mahler measures. Our proofs rely on Y. Bilu's equidistribution theorem and its effective version proved by C. D'Andrea \emph{et al.}, as well as on a method developed by P. Borwein \emph{et al.} While it is natural to consider Bilu's equidistribution results in conjunction with the Borwein {\it et al}. method to Lehmer's problem, we are not aware of any previous work in the literature that employs this particular approach.

entry.title: Squarefree Values of Random Polynomials
entry.summary: In this paper we consider the error term in the expected count of squarefree values of a polynomial when evaluated at integers \(n\le N\). We prove a power saving on average over polynomials of fixed degree and height at most \(H\). Our results improve previous estimates of Browning and Shparlinski in that the required range of \(H\) is independent of the degree, but depends on \(N\)

entry.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
entry.summary: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $λ_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}λ_1(f)^n$ if $λ_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $λ_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.

entry.title: Local obstructions and certified computations for perfect powers in power sums
entry.summary: Let $S_k(x)=1^k+\cdots+x^k$. We study perfect-power values of $S_k(x)$ by combining local valuations with finite congruence certificates. For an irregular Bernoulli pair $(p,r)$ with $e=v_p(B_r)\ge1$, we prove a valuation formula uniform for $k\equiv r+1\pmod{p^e(p-1)}$, subject to an explicit condition on $v_p(x(x+1))$. This gives explicit families of nonexistence results in which both $x$ and $k$ are unbounded. We also determine all solutions of $S_k(x)=y^n$ for $3\le x\le10^6$ with $x\equiv0,3\pmod4$, leaving $k$ and $n\ge2$ unrestricted and including squares. This extends Hajdu's fixed-$x$ classification in the same residue classes. A uniform restriction on the normalized odd part of $S_k(x)$ and finite certificates exclude every $k\ge6$; the remaining exponents are checked by exact integer arithmetic. The certificates admit independent verification. We further prove a limitation of congruence tests of bounded prime-power depth and solve the equation for every $x\equiv28\pmod{5\,110\,664}$.

entry.title: A secondary term in the first moment of cubic $L$-functions over function fields
entry.summary: Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power with $q\equiv2\pmod3$. We study the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\Fq(T)$, ordered by their genus. By averaging the rational sieve variable in the double Dirichlet series of Hong and Fang, we obtain meromorphic continuation beyond the secondary polar divisor. Combining this continuation with the cubic Gauss-sum residues computed by David, Florea and Lalín gives an explicit term of order $q^{5g/6}$, with a real coefficient depending on $g$ modulo $6$, and an error $O_{q,\eps}(q^{(23/28+\eps)g})$. The periodic coefficient is not identically zero. The proof uses an exact first difference supplied by the functional equation, an Euler product for the sieve average, and Bochner's tube theorem in the Dirichlet variables.

entry.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.

entry.title: On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms
entry.summary: We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.

entry.title: Two parametric $q$-supercongruences from Andrews' multi-series transformation
Rational Points on Affine Varieties over Finite Fields and Polygonal Number Sequences
entry.summary: Authors, in an earlier work, proved that prime power subsequences of the polygonal numbers corresponding to $4$, $6$, $8$, and $10$ arise naturally as the numbers of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of certain double Danielewski surfaces. In this work, authors generalize the previous construction and give a new family of affine varieties over finite fields such that the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of these varieties give the prime power subsequence of every polygonal number sequence.

entry.title: Traces of Green's functions on $\mathbb{H}^q$ over point-hypersurface pairs
entry.summary: The famous algebraicity conjecture of Gross and Zagier for the values at CM points of higher Green's functions was recently proven by Bruinier, Li and Yang. Motivated by this the values of the automorphic Green's function at pairs of special points in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ were studied by Herrero, Imamoglu, von Pippich and Schwagenscheidt, and an analogous algebraicity result for traces of Green's functions was established. In this paper, we consider higher automorphic Green's functions $G_{s}(P,Q)$ on hyperbolic $q$-space $\mathbb{H}^q$ for $q\geq 2$ when the spectral parameter $s$ is a positive even integer, and prove an explicit finite formula for their traces over geodesic hypersurfaces in one of the variables. This formula provides a geometric interpretation of the traces of Green's functions for every choice of a point in $\mathbb{H}^q$ for the second variable. As an application, we obtain rationality results when the second variable is evaluated at a special point providing further evidence that such results for traces of Green's functions do not depend on any underlying complex structure.

entry.title: Spectral convergence associated with Weil's quadratic form
entry.summary: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study a distinguished self-adjoint extension of the differentiation operator on a Hilbert space defined by the Weil quadratic form localized to a finite interval. The local quadratic form is determined by data from finitely many places, without requiring the zeros of the Riemann zeta function as input. We prove that the positive eigenvalues of this extension converge to the distinct positive ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function as the interval expands. We also prove that the associated normalized spectral entire functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane to the canonical product over these distinct ordinates. The key step is an identity expressing the inverse of the local extension as a compression of the inverse of a global self-adjoint operator.

entry.title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $Ξ$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
entry.summary: We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|κ|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $κ$. Fixed-point irrationality and exact Picard rank remain open. The heat tangent differs from the matched fixed-exponent isomonodromic direction, but admits a local moving-exponent curve lift. Separately, a reciprocal-head canopy certificate combined with published finite-RH and rectangular time-barrier verifications bounds the de Bruijn--Newman constant by $Λ\le433/2500=0.1732$ without a QRH assumption. These local arithmetic and global analytic results share a phase--transverse bridge; no equivalence between core nonresonance and RH is asserted.

entry.title: The Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic for primes $p$ and $p+4$ from a uniform zeta-ratios conjecture
entry.summary: We prove the Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of difference four from a restricted uniform two-over-two zeta-ratios formula. The formula has error $O_\varepsilon(U^{1/2+\varepsilon})$, real parts of all four shifts in $[3/64,5/64]$, and imaginary parts of absolute value at most $U^{1/4}$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,101/100)$, we obtain an error $O_\varepsilon(x^{-1/16+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_\varepsilon(x^{-3/8+\varepsilon})$. The proof retains the crossed zero residues in Mellin inversion and estimates their mixed term with the logarithmic-derivative integral. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference four. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_4$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted Möbius approximant in the Nyman--Beurling criterion by finite identities.

entry.title: Hausdorff dimension of canonical height spectra
entry.summary: We study the Hausdorff dimension of the closure of the canonical height values associated to finite compositions of two rational maps. For rational maps with common periodic critical points, a nonzero local--global height discrepancy gives a nonempty set of starting points with positive-dimensional spectra. For polynomials, equality of the normalized logarithms of the leading coefficients at every place forces dimension zero; a single-place discrepancy gives positive dimension under boundedness at the other places. We construct rational cubic pairs with spectra of dimension \(\log2/\log3\). The spectrum dimension gives a lower bound for the growth exponent of the number of distinct orbit points of bounded height. At the degree exponent, positive Hausdorff measure gives matching growth bounds for multiplicatively dependent degrees. For independent degrees, a restriction of the covering intervals and a Diophantine rotation estimate give a lower bound with logarithmic loss of exponent strictly less than \(1/2\). Quadratic monomial examples show that the spectrum dimension can depend on the starting point even when both individual orbits are infinite.

entry.title: The limiting zero counting measure for Eisenstein series
entry.summary: For an arbitrary congruence group $Γ$, we study the zeros of a generating set of the space of Eisenstein series of varying even weight for all $Γ(1)$-conjugates of $Γ$. These zeros form a $Γ(1)$-invariant set that descends to the modular orbifold $Y(1)$. It is known that, as the (even) weight tends to infinity, the set of zeros converges in the Hausdorff metric to finitely many geodesic segments. In this paper, we find the weak limit of the normalised counting measure of the zeros in the (natural) orbifold sense: if a geodesic occurring in the Hausdorff limit is parametrised by the unit circle $S^1$ via a Möbius transformation then the limit measure on this segment is the pullback of the Haar measure on $S^1$ by that transformation. For the proof, we first show a version of the Poincaré--Lelong theorem for orbifold curves, and then apply it on $Y(1)$ to reduce the problem to computing the scaled limit of the subharmonic functions $\log |E|$ associated to Eisenstein series $E$. This turns out to be the maximum of the negative logarithm of the modulus of finitely many linear functions supported on the relevant geodesic segments, and we finish the proof by showing that the associated measure has no atoms and making explicit, on each open segment, the distributional Laplacian of this function in terms of the argument measure. The non-atomicity allows us to conclude a sublinear growth rate in the weight for the total order of all Eisenstein series at a given point in $Y(1)$, and weak convergence also of the non-orbifold measure to the same limit.

entry.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
entry.summary: Finding the roots of a polynomial over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ in deterministic polynomial time is a long-standing open problem. Classical deterministic methods work in the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and are efficient only when $q-1$ is smooth, which is rarely the case. We propose a method that replaces $\mathbb F_q^\times$ by the groups of rational points of an elliptic curve $E$ and of its quadratic twist $\widetilde E$. The computation splits into an offline phase, which depends only on $\mathbb F_q$ and outputs a short \emph{elliptic preprocessing datum} $\mathcal D$, and an online phase, which processes the input polynomial. Writing $Ξ(\mathcal D)$ for the largest prime factor of $\lvert E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert\cdot\lvert\widetilde E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert$, the online phase is deterministic and finds the roots of any $f\in\mathbb F_q[X]$ of degree $n$ within $\widetilde O(Ξ(\mathcal D)^2\,n\log^2 q+n^ω\log q+n\log^3 q)$ operations in $\mathbb F_q$. A precursor of our method is an algorithm by Rónyai, which recovers the roots through Galois computations over number fields, relies on GRH, and comes with a polynomial bound of unspecified degree; in contrast, our online phase works entirely over $\mathbb F_q$ and is unconditional. Moreover, $\mathcal D$ can be certified deterministically and unconditionally in time polynomial in $\log q$ and $Ξ(\mathcal D)$. We conjecture that every $\mathbb F_q$ of large enough characteristic admits a datum with $Ξ(\mathcal D)\leq(\log q)^{O(1)}$, and support this with a heuristic and with experiments. Constructing such a datum in polynomial time remains open.

entry.title: Binary Quadratic Forms, Shintani Lifts, and Twisted L-Values
entry.summary: Let $F\in S_{2k}^{new}(M,χ^2)$ be a Hecke newform, and $D$ a fundamental discriminant with $(-1)χ(-1)D>0$. Via the Shimura Correspondence, we get associated modular forms of half-integral weight, and Waldspurger showed that for such $g=\sum c_nq^n \in S_{k+1/2}(4M',χ;F)$, if $c_{|D|}(g)\neq 0$, then $|c_{|D|}(g)|^2 \propto |D|^{k-1/2}L(F\otimes \overlineχ\otimes χ_D,k)$. Kohnen refined this in the case that $f\in S_{2k}^{new}(N)$ for $N$ odd and squarefree, making explicit $|c_{|D|}(g)|^2$ for $g \in S^+_{k+1/2}(4N;f)$. However, $c_{|D|}(g)=0$ unless $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=w_p(f)$ for all $p|N$. In this paper, we produce more generally $g \in S^+_{k+1/2}(4\ \mathrm{lcm}(N,N_1^2),χ;f\otimes χ)$, where $χ$ is a character of odd squarefree conductor $N_1$, using a family of generalised Shimura/Shintani maps $Ψ_χ^D,{Ψ_χ^D}^*$ due to Kojima and Tokuno. Extending their work (and Kohnen's), we compute its Petersson norm, and give an explicit formula for all the $|c_m(g)|^2$. The key technical ingredient is an explicit set of representatives for $L^0_{M_1,M}(M_1^2D^2)/Γ_0(M)$ of binary quadratic forms. We also use a new multiplicity-one result based on work of Kohnen, Ueda, and Waldspurger. In the case $N_1|N$, we reconstruct forms previously considered by Baruch-Mao and Prasanna, which change Kohnen's condition to $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=-w_p(f)$ for all $p|N_1$, thus relating twisted $L$-values to squares of Fourier coefficients for all classes of discriminants.

entry.title: Partial rigidity and q-additive functions
entry.summary: A system $(X,μ, T)$ is partially rigid with constant $δ>0$ if there exists an incresing sequence $(n_k)$ such that $\displaystyle \liminf_{k \to \infty } μ(A \cap T^{-n_k}A) \geq δμ(A)$ for every measurable $A \subset X$. The partial rigidity rate is the largest constant of partial rigidity. We characterize the partial rigidity rate of subshifts arising from $q$-additive functions $\pmod M$ in terms of quantities arising from Bésineau's theorem. With this, we build a family of strongly $q$-additive functions to deduce that the collection of partial rigidity rates for substitution subshifts is dense in $[0,1]$ answering a question of Donoso, Maass and the author.

entry.title: Shintani Cocycle Decomposition of Topological Polylogarithms for Totally Real Fields
entry.summary: We compare two cohomological constructions computing special values of partial zeta functions of totally real number fields at nonpositive integers: the Shintani cocycles arising from polyhedral cone decompositions, and the Eisenstein classes obtained from the topological polylogarithm. In particular we prove that the specialization of the topological polylogarithm at a nonzero torsion point coincides in cohomology with the Shintani class up to an explicit sign and error term, and obtain Siegel and Klingen's classical rationality Theorem.
entry.arxiv:comment: 32 pages, based on author's PhD thesis

entry.title: Prime Numbers of the Form $24m+1$ and Erdös-Straus Conjecture
entry.summary: In 1948, Erdös and Straus formulated a conjecture on Egyptian fractions. One only needs to prove the conjecture for any prime number $n$ such that $n\equiv 1\;(\mbox{mod}\;24)$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient polynomial condition for a number of the form $24m+1$ to be a prime number. Then we present 56 solvability polynomials consisting of our earlier tame solutions, wild solutions and the polynomials for composite numbers of the form $24m+1$. Numeric test shows that they imply the conjecture. Moreover, we give a list of 36 exponential-polynomial functions consisting of our earlier 28 tame solutions and the polynomials for composite numbers, whose numeric test shows that Howerton's conjecture on fourteen wild primes holds. Furthermore, we find a version of Goldbach conjecture modulo 24.

entry.title: Value-distribution of Euler--Zagier type multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments on the critical line
entry.summary: We consider the value-distribution of the Euler--Zagier type multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments on the critical line. Mishou showed that the set of the values of the Euler--Zagier double sum with identical arguments on the critical line is dense in the complex plane under the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper, we generalize Mishou's result to the $r$-fold Euler--Zagier multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments for $r geq 4$.

entry.title: A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
entry.summary: Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erdős and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators. Dixmier subsequently proved their conjecture $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_n^2/(n-1)$, a bound depending only on $a_n$ and $n$ that removes the factor $2$ from the corresponding quadratic estimate. Following the Erdős--Graham approach, we remove the factor $2$ while retaining the dependence on $a_{n-1}$, and prove $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_{n-1}\lceil a_n/(n-1)\rceil-a_n-1$. This bound can be substantially smaller than Dixmier's when $a_{n-1}$ is small relative to $a_n$. For every $n\ge3$, we also construct infinitely many instances satisfying the reverse inequality, which shows that the bound is sharp.

entry.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
entry.summary: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.

entry.title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
entry.summary: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive. This gives rise to a lower bound of the $m-$index of the Ehrhart polynomial.

entry.title: An explicit bound on $|ζ_K(1+it)|$
entry.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n$ and discriminant $Δ$. The estimate $|ζ_K(1+it)|\le C_K\log{t}$, where $C_K$ is an unspecified constant depending on $K$, is a well--known result in the literature. We obtain an explicit upper bound for $|ζ_K(1+it)|$, depending only on $n$ and $Δ$. We also show how improvements on the bound depend on improvements on estimates of the ideal counting function $I_K$ and the residue of $ζ_K$ at $s=1$.

entry.title: Trivial Iwasawa modules and arithmetic linking numbers
entry.summary: We give a computable criterion of the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa module over the maximal multiple $\mathbb Z_p$-extension of a number filed in which an odd prime number $p$ splits completely. This criterion is obtained from the description of the presentation matrix of the Galois coinvariant of the Iwasawa module by arithmetic linking numbers. The description is based on the Koch type presentation of a pro-$p$ Galois group with restricted ramification, which is analogous to the Milnor presentation of a link group from a viewpoint of arithmetic topology.

entry.title: On the unit group of some triquadratic fields
entry.summary: In this paper, we calculate the unit groups and the $2$-class numbers of the fields $ \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{q}, \sqrt{rs})$, where $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $r$ and $s$ are distinct prime numbers satisfying some congruent conditions. As an application of our main results, we derive the precise 2-class number for each field in our family. Furthermore, we show that Greenberg's conjecture is verified for several infinite families of real biquadratic fields.

entry.title: Elliptic curve rank growth in multi-quadratic extensions
entry.summary: In this article we give an algorithm to produce infinitely many explicit quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a rational point and fixed root number. Moreover, under the Parity Conjecture (or other technical hypotheses), for each $n\geq 1$, we produce explicit multi-quadratic extensions $L_n$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, of degree $2^n$, such that the growth in rank from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $L_n$ is at least $\max\{2n+2^{n-1}-1,\,2^n-1\}$ when the root number of $E$ is $-1$, and at least $\max\{2n,\,2^{n-1}\}$ when it is $+1$. As a result, assuming Parity, we exhibit elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ and extensions of degree $2^n$ where the rank after base-extension is greater than or equal to $34$ or $30+\max\{2n+2^{n-1},\,2^n\}$.

entry.title: On Parameterization of Some Problems in Number Theory
entry.summary: The article is devoted to the parametric solution of some Diophantine equations with two variables. In essence, we find an additional parametric relationship between the solution of the original equation and the simpler linear equation ax - by = 1. The method of hidden parameters helps to obtain a parametric representation of integer solutions for a number of problems in number theory. The method consists in that, first, instead of each quantity included in the original equation, we introduce an additional number of parameters using a linear or non-linear function, which allows us to find both connections between the parameters and some parametric solution of the desired equation. Then we reset (nullify) the introduced linear or non-linear functional dependence (hidden parameters), which in the original formulation of the problem would mean just changing the letter designation of the parameters. However, as a result of these actions, a simplified parametric solution is obtained and the found relationship between the parameters remains. In this paper, the method is discussed in detail using the example of parametric solving such Diophantine equation as the Pell equation. The method of such parameterization is also applied to problems related to Pell's equation. The methods of parameterization are discussed for the Delaunay equation, the Nagell equation and similar equations of higher powers.

entry.title: Quantitative nodal domain count for Maass forms
entry.summary: We consider a real even Hecke-Maass cusp form $φ$ on the modular surface, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. We prove that its restriction to any fixed compact segment $β$ of the vertical geodesic above $i$ has $\gg_{β,\varepsilon} T^{1/6-\varepsilon}$ sign changes, yielding the same lower bound for the number of distinct inert nodal domains meeting the segment. Building on ideas of Jang-Jung and Jung-Young, we study correlations between values at points on the vertical geodesic separated by distances of order $T^{-1}$. Using arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity and Dirichlet-polynomial estimates, we show that the correlation is negative for a suitable choice of separation. An elementary counting argument and the Iwaniec-Sarnak supremum bound then give the claimed lower bound.

entry.title: Divisor Sums with Spacing Constraints
entry.summary: For $x,y>0$ let $S(x,y)$ denote the largest value of $\sum_{n\in A}τ(n)$ over subsets $A$ of $[1,x]\cap\N$ whose elements are pairwise separated by more than $y$ (here $τ$ is the divisor function). We determine the order of magnitude, and in a subrange the precise asymptotic, of $S(x,y)$ when the spacing parameter $y$ ranges over a polylogarithmic scale $y=(\log x)^{1+λ(\logλ-1)}$, $λ>1$. We show that for every fixed $λ>2$ the spacing constraint costs a computable power of $\log x$ in the exponent, while for every fixed $1<λ<2$ it costs nothing at all: $S(x,y)\sim x\log x$, the same asymptotic as the unconstrained sum $\sum_{n\le x}τ(n)$. Near the threshold $λ=2$ the two regimes meet, and we show that for any fixed $κ>0,$ $S(x,y)\asymp_κ x\log x$ uniformly as long as $λ\le 2+2κ/\sqrt{\log\log x}$. The proof combines the Sathe-Selberg distribution of the number of prime factors, a smooth squarefree estimate obtained from a generating function together with Cauchy's formula, a sieve estimate for correlations among the squarefree parts of the integers that contribute most heavily to $\sum_{n\le x}τ(n)$, and two combinatorial devices (the Caro-Wei bound and a concentration inequality on the symmetric group) used to extract a well-spaced independent set from a sparse auxiliary graph.

entry.title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
entry.summary: We describe a new family of Dirichlet L-functions that provably have an unusual value distribution. Experimentally, we find that the L-functions in this family have a significant and previously undetected bias in the distribution of gaps between their zeros. These phenomena appear to have an arithmetic explanation that corresponds to the nonvanishing of a certain Gauss-type sum. We give a complete classification of the characters for which this sum is nonzero and count them. This sum vanishes for 100% of primitive Dirichlet characters, so L-functions in our newly discovered family are rare (a set of density zero among all primitive characters). The nonvanishing of this sum implies that there is a main term when one integrates the Z-function associated to a Dirichlet L-function over a long interval. We prove that the L-functions in this family are the only GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q cuspidal automorphic L-functions whose Z-functions have a "large" mean value when integrated. We discuss analogous results for the Riemann zeta-function.
entry.arxiv:comment: 38 pages, 13 figures, including a short appendix

entry.title: Nonvanishing of 2-primary Kolyvagin classes via simultaneous quadratic twists
entry.summary: Let $E/\mathbf{Q}$ be an elliptic curve, let $K=\mathbf{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ satisfy the Heegner hypothesis with $D<-4$, and fix a modular parametrization $\varphi$ with $\varphi(\infty)=O$. Under surjectivity modulo $2^L$, with $L\ge 2$, and a cohomological exclusion condition at level $4$, we construct a finite set of primes $T$ such that, writing $d_T=\prod_{q\in T}(-q)$ and $n_T=\prod_{q\in T}q$, the $2$-Selmer dimensions of $E^{d_T}$ and $E^{d_TD}$ are $0$ and $1$. The support size is bounded in terms of the initial Selmer dimensions, independently of $L$. Inspired by the work of Tian and Tian--Yuan--Zhang on congruent numbers, we construct a point $Q_T$ on the terminal twist and identify its Kummer class with the standard mod-$2$ Kolyvagin class. Using the low-corank $2$-converse and the $2$-primary Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, we prove that its index $m_T$ in the full Mordell--Weil lattice satisfies $v_2(m_T)=v_2(c_\varphi)+\mathfrak{i}(E,K)$. The optimal Manin constant theorem supplies a $2$-indivisible parametrization $\varphi_0$, for which $κ^{\mathrm{std}}_{n_T,1}(\varphi_0)\ne 0$ if and only if $\mathfrak{i}(E,K)=0$. When the intrinsic index vanishes, the minimum terminal support size is $R=\min\{d_2(E),d_2(E^D)\}$, and the normalized standard classes have order $2^M$ for $1\le M\le L$. Full $2$-adic Galois image then gives strong nonvanishing.

entry.title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},μ_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.

entry.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
entry.summary: Let $u$ be a received word for the full-length Reed--Solomon code $\operatorname{RS}_q(k)$, with interpolation polynomial $f_u$ of degree $k+m$. For each $m\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, we classify all such deep holes over every finite field, without a field-size hypothesis. None occur for odd $m$ in this range. At $m=4$ and $m=6$, the only exceptions are, respectively, the Segre sextic and Frobenius-power families; these occur only in dimension two over fields of characteristic two. For arbitrary $m\geqslant3$, we also establish two uniform bounds. If $\sqrt q\geqslant12(m+1)\log(2m+2)$, no word of interpolation degree $k+m$ is a deep hole when $q$ is odd, $k\geqslant3$, or $m$ is odd. If $q>16(m+2)^4$, we obtain the corresponding complete classification at every admissible $k$, including the explicit dimension-two exceptions. Our proofs use an agreement criterion expressed in complete homogeneous symmetric functions, agreement-count estimates, finite geometry, permutation-polynomial restrictions, and subset constructions for solving the resulting symmetric-function equations. The remaining finite cases are settled by finite computations with supplied certificates and deterministic verification programs.

entry.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
entry.summary: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.

entry.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
entry.summary: Let $k$ be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension $F/k$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ_{F/k})$ satisfies $(1-β)\log d_F\ge c(k)$ with an effective constant $c(k)>0$, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions $K$ of $k$, in the form $h_K R_K \ge c(k)\, d_K^{1/2}/((2π)^{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\log d_K)$. Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem excluded the fields with quadratic subfields, since those subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field $k$, the first result removes this obstruction. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let $K/k$ be a Galois extension with group $G$, and suppose $S\subset G$ contains the identity. For any prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $k$, let $δ_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the proportion of the primes of $K$ above $\mathfrak{p}$ whose Frobenius lies in $S$. Then $\sum_{N\mathfrak{p}\le X}δ_{\mathfrak{p}}\,\log N\mathfrak{p}/N\mathfrak{p}\le(|S|/|G|+\varepsilon)\log X+O(1)$ holds uniformly in $K$ as soon as $X\ge d_K^{C}$, with $C$ and the implied constant depending only on $\varepsilon$, $C$, and the degree $[K:\mathbb{Q}]$. The proof is the argument of OpenAI in the form given by Kerr, simple vanishing at the points $(ιθ)_{ι\in S}$, with $θ$ in a box in $\mathcal{O}_K$, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be $[K:\mathbb{Q}]/|S|$ by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the determinant method gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.
